limits: ESP is encrypted: the cipher, tunnel or transport mode, and the inner packets are estimates from packet sizes, never read from the packet. Families with equal IV, ICV and alignment (AES-GCM, AES-CCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) cannot be told apart.
Padding is assumed minimal (no TFC padding); an implementation that pads more makes the inner sizes smaller than the bounds shown.
Tunnel versus transport mode cannot be read from sizes alone; both are computed. The IKE exchange that agreed the mode is encrypted (IKEv2 IKE_AUTH, IKEv1 Quick Mode).

limits: Only what crossed this capture point is visible: a Fragmentation Needed sent towards a host on another segment, or dropped by an ACL before this point, is invisible here, so a black hole verdict means 'no ICMP seen here', not proof that no router sent one.
A vanished probe can be loss rather than MTU; the black hole verdict needs smaller probes to the same destination answered and larger ones never answered.
Fragments captured on one side of the reassembling host show whether pieces arrived here; whether the host reassembled them is not visible.
IPv6 extension headers (including fragment headers) are not decoded.

limits: ESP hides the inner header: from one capture the inner DSCP of encrypted traffic is unknown, so 'copied' is inferred from several markings on one SA. Compare an inside and an outside capture with correlate_captures to see the rewrite directly.

RTP latency is not measurable from one capture point; jitter and loss are what arrived here. RTP is found by its header shape, so a non-RTP UDP flow that looks like RTP for 10+ packets can be counted.
Clock rate is 8000 Hz for static audio payload types and estimated from timestamps for dynamic ones.

limits: Retransmissions, gaps and RTT are what this capture point saw: a segment lost after the capture point shows as a retransmission here, one lost before it shows as a gap. RTT is from the capture point to the receiver and back, not end to end unless the capture was taken on the sender.
A connection whose handshake was not captured has no window scale, so window-full checks and options are skipped for it.
Payload contents are not judged here (see the tls detector for TLS handshakes).

Only the cleartext handshake is read. In TLS 1.3 everything after the ServerHello is encrypted: the certificate, the server's extensions and any later alert cannot be seen. In TLS 1.2 and older the certificate is visible and is read here.
Certificate trust (chain to a trusted root, revocation) is not judged; only what the certificate says.
In TLS 1.3 the server's ALPN choice travels in the encrypted EncryptedExtensions message, so server_chose.alpn is null and an ALPN baseline is checked only for TLS 1.2 and older.
With Encrypted Client Hello the visible SNI is the outer, public name, not the real server name.
A handshake split across segments is reassembled from the first bytes of each direction; one that starts before the capture, or whose segments were lost before the capture point, cannot be read.
QUIC, DTLS and STARTTLS are not decoded.
